risk_if_not_implemented: Without Standardized Terminology, security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, no risk is rated Likely; risks rated Possible include Failure to Support Business / Mission Objectives (R-GV-1), Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities (R-GV-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources.
compensating_control_1.justification: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation) (NET-06) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Standardized Terminology (GOV-03.2) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Alignment With Enterprise Architecture
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to develop an enterprise architecture, aligned with industry-recognized leading practices, with consideration for security, compliance and resilience principles that addresses risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals and other organizations.
compensating_control_2.justification: Alignment With Enterprise Architecture (SEA-04) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Standardized Terminology (GOV-03.2) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
